title: How We’re Coping One Year into the Pandemic, with Vaile Wright, PhD

sentences.en: When the COVID-19 pandemic was declared in March 2020, many people headed home to shelter-in-place
sentences.zh: 当COVID-19大流行在2020年3月宣布时，许多人回家进行居家隔离

sentences.en: and expected that they would return to their offices and schools within a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 并期望在几周内就能回到办公室和学校。

sentences.en: None of us could have imagined how different the world would look one year later, especially that more than 500,000 Americans and 2.5 million people around the world
sentences.zh: 我们谁也没有想到一年后的世界会发生如此大的变化，特别是超过50万美国人和全球250万人

sentences.en: would die from complications of COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 将死于COVID-19的并发症。

sentences.en: Along with the physical toll of the coronavirus, the pandemic's economic and social consequences
sentences.zh: 除了冠状病毒造成的身体伤害外，大流行带来的经济和社会后果

sentences.en: have caused what some people are calling a second pandemic of mental health concerns
sentences.zh: 已经引发了一些人所称的心理健康问题的第二场大流行

sentences.en: as Americans have dealt with lost jobs, lack of child care, social isolation, and the illness and death of loved ones.
sentences.zh: 因为美国人一直在应对失业、缺乏托儿服务、社交隔离以及亲人的病痛和离世。

sentences.en: APA's Stress in America survey has been tracking this mental health toll over the course of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 美国心理协会（APA）的“美国压力调查”一直在整个大流行期间追踪这一心理健康代价。

sentences.en: Where are we now?
sentences.zh: 我们现在处于什么位置？

sentences.en: How is our mental and our physical health one year in?
sentences.zh: 经历了一年之后，我们的心理和身体健康状况如何？

sentences.en: Now that vaccines are providing some hope for an end to the pandemic, how are we feeling about returning to our pre-pandemic lives?
sentences.zh: 既然疫苗为结束大流行带来了一些希望，我们对回归大流行前的生活有何感想？

sentences.en: And what can each of us do that is healthy to ease our stress and anxiety in the face of continuing uncertainty about the future?
sentences.zh: 面对对未来的持续不确定性，我们每个人能做些什么健康的举措来缓解压力和焦虑？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是美国心理协会的旗舰播客，探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Vail Wright, a clinical psychologist and the Senior Director of Healthcare Innovation here at APA.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是维尔·赖特博士，她是一名临床心理学家，也是APA医疗创新高级总监。

sentences.en: As a spokesperson for the association, Dr. Wright has given more than 100 interviews over the past year
sentences.zh: 作为协会的发言人，赖特博士在过去一年里接受了100多次采访

sentences.en: about the mental health consequences of COVID-19, including stress, anxiety, and loneliness, and offered advice on how to cope and build resilience.
sentences.zh: 内容涉及COVID-19对心理健康的影响，包括压力、焦虑和孤独，并就如何应对和建立韧性提出了建议。

sentences.en: She has been a calm and reassuring voice to many as she has offered evidence-based advice
sentences.zh: 她一直是许多人平静而令人安心的声音，她提供了基于证据的建议

sentences.en: on how to navigate the challenges we have all faced during this most unusual and stressful year.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们如何度过在这个极其不寻常且充满压力的年份中我们都面临的挑战。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Wright.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天加入我们，赖特博士。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: I just mentioned our Stress in America survey in the introduction.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚在开场白中提到了我们的“美国压力调查”。

sentences.en: We have a new report coming out on March 11th with fresh data on how Americans' physical and mental health have fared over the past year.
sentences.zh: 我们在3月11日发布了一份新报告，其中包含关于美国人在过去一年中身心健康状况的最新数据。

sentences.en: Can you tell us in general terms what it found?
sentences.zh: 你能总体上告诉我们它发现了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, what we found in this report was that, you know, going a year now into this pandemic and adults are consistently reporting extremely high levels of stress
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我们在这次报告中发现的是，进入这场大流行的一年时间里，成年人们持续报告着极高的压力水平

sentences.en: and that this is actually leading to engaging in some pretty unhealthy coping behaviors in order to manage that stress.
sentences.zh: 并且这实际上导致他们为了管理压力而采取了一些相当不健康的应对行为。

sentences.en: And that certainly has us really concerned.
sentences.zh: 这确实让我们感到非常担忧。

sentences.en: And so what are the outcomes then?
sentences.zh: 那么结果是什么呢？

sentences.en: If they're engaging in unhealthy behaviors, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 如果他们正在从事不健康的行为什么情况会发生？

sentences.en: So what we're seeing is people are reporting undesired weight changes, probably related to unhealthy eating habits, disrupted sleep, being less active,
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到的是，人们报告了不期望的体重变化，这可能与不健康的饮食习惯、睡眠被打乱、活动减少有关，

sentences.en: and one of the most concerning is increases in alcohol intake.
sentences.zh: 其中最令人担忧的之一是酒精摄入量的增加。

sentences.en: And when you take these together, they start to form a pattern of the ways in which people just are not,
sentences.zh: 当你把这些放在一起考虑时，它们开始形成一种模式，表明人们不仅

sentences.en: A, following the advice we're trying to give them, but are really, you know, just failing to engage in the kinds of behaviors we would hope to shore up their emotional well-being.
sentences.zh: A，没有遵循我们试图给他们的建议，而且真的是，你知道的，未能采取我们所希望的能够巩固其情绪健康的那些行为。

sentences.en: And if this continues, the greatest concern, of course, is that it could lead to long-term negative physical and mental health consequences.
sentences.zh: 如果这种情况继续下去，最大的担忧当然是它可能导致长期的身体和心理健康负面后果。

sentences.en: Have these outcomes been distributed evenly across groups or are there particular groups of people or members of specific demographics that have been having a more difficult time this year?
sentences.zh: 这些结果在各个群体中分布均匀吗，还是有特定的群体或特定人口统计学的成员今年过得更艰难？

sentences.en: You know, since the beginning of the pandemic, we've really seen, again, this consistent pattern of four really vulnerable groups.
sentences.zh: 你知道，自大流行开始以来，我们确实再次看到了这四个真正弱势群体的持续模式。

sentences.en: Those groups are parents with children under the age of 18, individuals from communities of color, essential workers, including frontline health care workers, and younger adults.
sentences.zh: 这些群体是：育有18岁以下孩子的父母、有色人种社区的个人、包括一线医护人员在内的核心员工，以及年轻成年人。

sentences.en: These four groups are just reporting some of the worst outcomes, and certainly are individuals that we as a country need to be concerned about.
sentences.zh: 这四个群体报告的结果最差，绝对是我们作为一个国家需要关注的个人。

sentences.en: For those listeners who might recognize themselves in some of these statistical areas that we're talking about,
sentences.zh: 对于那些可能在我们正在谈论的这些统计数据中看到自己的听众，

sentences.en: what should they do to adopt more healthy habits and cope in more healthy and productive ways?
sentences.zh: 他们应该怎么做才能养成更健康的习惯并以更健康、更有成效的方式应对？

sentences.en: Well, I think the first needs to come from a sense of awareness, an awareness that no matter what your situation is,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为首先需要有一种意识，一种无论你的情况如何的意识，

sentences.en: nobody's immune to what's happening right now, and that this is stressful.
sentences.zh: 没有人能免受当前正在发生的事情的影响，而且这确实压力很大。

sentences.en: And if we can kind of just acknowledge that things are stressful and that we can legitimately feel that way,
sentences.zh: 如果我们能某种程度上只是承认事情确实很有压力，并且我们可以合理地有这种感受，

sentences.en: I think that actually opens up some space to really identify, okay, what is one or two areas that I could start making small changes?
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上为真正确定“好吧，我可以在哪一两个方面开始做出小改变”腾出了一些空间。

sentences.en: And then it's about kind of thinking about what those things are.
sentences.zh: 然后就是考虑这些事情是什么。

sentences.en: We often beat ourselves up because we aren't successful at our goals because we only rely on our willpower, as if we can just will ourselves into changing behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们经常因为达不到目标而自我责备，因为我们只依靠意志力，就好像我们可以仅凭意志力来改变行为一样。

sentences.en: And really what we need to do is change our environments, put behavioral goals in place that are really attainable, and then we can build off of those small successes.
sentences.zh: 而我们真正需要做的是改变我们的环境，制定真正可以实现的切实行为目标，然后我们可以以这些小的成功为基础继续前进。

sentences.en: What about the parents of young school-age children who are among the most stressed out but also the most pressed for time?
sentences.zh: 那些压力最大但时间也最紧迫的学龄前儿童的父母呢？

sentences.en: Is there any special advice for them?
sentences.zh: 有什么给他们的特殊建议吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think parents really need to do a couple different things.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为父母确实需要做几件不同的事情。

sentences.en: One is, are you asking for help from the right people and at the right times?
sentences.zh: 一个是，你是否在正确的时间向正确的人寻求帮助？

sentences.en: Are there things that maybe your kids could be doing that they're not?
sentences.zh: 有没有可能是你的孩子本可以做却没有做的事情？

sentences.en: Like some small developmentally appropriate chores around the house to take some of that burden off?
sentences.zh: 比如在家里做一些适合他们年龄的能分担部分负担的小家务？

sentences.en: Is your partner, if you have one, are you on the same page about who should be doing what and how to trade off tasks
sentences.zh: 你的伴侣（如果你有的话），你们是否就谁该做什么以及如何分工达成了一致，

sentences.en: and how to, you know, have each other's back when somebody needs to take a break?
sentences.zh: 以及当某人需要休息时，如何（你知道的）互相支持？

sentences.en: And then you need to ask yourself, are there some things I can let go of?
sentences.zh: 然后你需要问自己，有没有什么事情是我可以放下的？

sentences.en: Whether that's unrealistic expectations, so how you should be feeling, or concerns about too much device time, even though that may be a lifesaver for you right now,
sentences.zh: 不管是关于你应该有什么感觉的不切实际的期望，还是对花太多时间看电子设备的担忧（尽管这现在可能是你的救命稻草），

sentences.en: and just maybe saying no to some of the things that really you can let go of.
sentences.zh: 也许只是对那些你确实可以放下的事情说不。

sentences.en: So how do we change our environment in ways that will make it easier for us to do things that are healthy?
sentences.zh: 那么我们如何以使我们更容易做健康事情的方式改变我们的环境呢？

sentences.en: Well, we have to sort of identify where some of our problem areas are, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们得找出我们的一些问题所在，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you're that kind of person that you know is maybe having that extra glass of wine in the evening, that making you uncomfortable, try not keeping so much wine in the house.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是那种你知道晚上可能会多喝一杯葡萄酒、这让你感到不舒服的人，试着不要在家里存那么多酒。

sentences.en: If it's not there, it's really hard to actually engage in it.
sentences.zh: 如果它不在那儿，你就很难去做了。

sentences.en: If you're having trouble sleeping, whether that's going to bed at a regular time, set yourself an alarm.
sentences.zh: 如果你有睡眠问题，不管是能不能在固定时间上床睡觉，给自己定个闹钟。

sentences.en: An alarm about an hour before you'd think is the bite time for you to go to sleep, so you can start winding down.
sentences.zh: 在认为是你睡觉的最佳时间大约一小时前定个闹钟，这样你就可以开始放松了。

sentences.en: That means turning off devices and maybe doing some soothing activities and just preparing yourself for sleep.
sentences.zh: 这意味着关掉电子设备，也许做一些舒缓的活动，为睡眠做好准备。

sentences.en: Similar in the morning, if you're hitting the snooze button over and over and over again,
sentences.zh: 早上也一样，如果你一次又一次地按贪睡按钮，

sentences.en: put your phone or your alarm far away from your bed so that you actually have to get up and go turn it off.
sentences.zh: 把你的手机或闹钟放在远离你床的地方，这样你实际上必须起床去把它关掉。

sentences.en: So those are the kinds of behavioral things we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是我们所说的行为方面的事情。

sentences.en: It's really helpful if you can incorporate others in your goals as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你能把别人也纳入你的目标中，那真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: So finding somebody who, like you, maybe wants to get out of the house a bit more and take walks.
sentences.zh: 所以找一个像你一样可能想多出门走走并散步的人。

sentences.en: Can you guys put that on your schedule and then adhere to it?
sentences.zh: 你们能把这安排在日程上然后坚持下去吗？

sentences.en: You know, really agree to meet because you know that the other person is depending on you.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，真正同意见面，因为你知道另一个人在指望你。

sentences.en: So those are the kinds of things that you can start off small and, again,
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是你可以从小事做起的事情，而且，

sentences.en: have some decent successes that can build on each other and make you feel like you can be even more effective.
sentences.zh: 取得一些不错的成功，这些成功可以相互叠加，让你觉得自己可以更有效率。

sentences.en: What about people who have been trying to work their way out of these behaviors and they're just not succeeding?
sentences.zh: 那些一直试图摆脱这些行为但就是没有成功的人呢？

sentences.en: How do they know when it's time to reach for outside help?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么知道什么时候该寻求外部帮助？

sentences.en: You know, historically, we've always said that the red flag to reach for outside help was when your feelings
sentences.zh: 你知道，从历史上看，我们总是说寻求外部帮助的危险信号是当你的感受

sentences.en: and your behaviors are really interfering with your ability to function in a significant way.
sentences.zh: 和你的行为在很大程度上真正干扰了你的日常功能时。

sentences.en: So typically, that means, you know, really being unable to work or not being very effective at work,
sentences.zh: 所以通常这意味着，你知道的，真的无法工作或在工作中效率不高，

sentences.en: not being able to take care of yourself or your kids, or if you're a young adult, not being able to go to school.
sentences.zh: 无法照顾自己或孩子，或者如果你是一个年轻人，无法去学校。

sentences.en: But I think at this point, we really need to revise that advice and just say at any point and at any time,
sentences.zh: 但我想在这一点上，我们真的需要修改这个建议，只需说在任何时候，

sentences.en: it's perfectly acceptable to go seek out professional help, in particular in these sorts of areas around behaviors,
sentences.zh: 去寻求专业帮助都是完全可以接受的，特别是在这些行为相关的领域，

sentences.en: because psychologists can really help you identify what are those steps that need to be taken in order to be more effective
sentences.zh: 因为心理学家真的可以帮助你确定需要采取哪些步骤才能更有效率，

sentences.en: and then, again, can hold you accountable because they'll follow up and see how you're doing and then help troubleshoot with you on how to make different changes.
sentences.zh: 然后，再次强调，可以让你承担责任，因为他们会跟进并查看你的情况，然后与你一起解决如何做出不同改变的问题。

sentences.en: And, yes, sometimes we can do that on our own, but what's really beneficial from a professional is that,
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，有时我们可以靠自己做到这一点，但从专业人士那里获得的真正好处是，

sentences.en: one, all the time gets to be about you.
sentences.zh: 第一，所有的时间都完全是关于你的。

sentences.en: It's not a reciprocal relationship, so you don't actually have to worry about how they feel.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种互惠的关系，所以你实际上不必担心他们的感受。

sentences.en: And so that really allows you to focus on yourself and to get the help that you need.
sentences.zh: 因此，这确实能让你专注于自己并获得所需的帮助。

sentences.en: As one of APA's leading spokespeople throughout the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 作为APA在大流行期间的主要发言人之一，

sentences.en: you've talked to many, many reporters about some of the coping behaviors that they've been hearing about and observing.
sentences.zh: 你与许多许多记者谈论过他们听到的和观察到的一些应对行为。

sentences.en: What are some of the more creative behaviors you've encountered through the course of the year?
sentences.zh: 在这一年的时间里，你遇到过哪些更具创意的行为？

sentences.en: I think certainly I've heard of a fair amount of different sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 我想我当然听说过相当多各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: Obviously, stress baking was the large story for a while.
sentences.zh: 很明显，因压力而烘焙曾是一段时间内的大新闻。

sentences.en: You know, I kind of enjoyed talking with people about this nostalgic feeling that people have,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我挺喜欢跟人们聊聊人们怀旧的这种感觉，

sentences.en: that they want to watch old movies and old TV shows and listen to old music from their childhood to bring them back to happier times.
sentences.zh: 他们想看老电影、老电视剧，听童年的老音乐，把他们带回更快乐的时光。

sentences.en: I think for me, one of the more interesting developments has been around this concept of Zoom fatigue.
sentences.zh: 我想对我来说，更有趣的发展之一是围绕“Zoom疲劳”这个概念。

sentences.en: And the ways in which technology can play a pretty significant role, but how also it isn't a panacea, and we can't overly rely on it to fix everything.
sentences.zh: 技术可以发挥相当大的作用，但它也不是万灵药，我们不能过分依赖它来解决一切。

sentences.en: One of my favorite research studies that's come out is that people talk 15% louder on Zoom calls and video conferencing calls, and that it takes that much more energy.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的出炉的研究之一是，人们在Zoom通话和视频会议通话中说话声音会大15%，这需要付出更多的精力。

sentences.en: And that's part of what contributes to that Zoom fatigue.
sentences.zh: 这也是导致这种Zoom疲劳的部分原因。

sentences.en: And in our household, the joke is that I talk much louder than 15% when I'm on my Zoom calls and drive everybody pretty crazy.
sentences.zh: 在我们家里，开玩笑的说法是，当我进行Zoom通话时，我说话的声音比15%还要大得多，把大家都快逼疯了。

sentences.en: You know, Zoom is a challenge in itself because if you were in a meeting with people, you could talk over each other, you could have side conversations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，Zoom本身就是一个挑战，因为如果你和人们开会，你可以压过别人的声音说话，你可以进行私下交谈。

sentences.en: And Zoom doesn't let you do that.
sentences.zh: 而Zoom不容许你这样做。

sentences.en: So it's really, in a sense, imposing a kind of discipline on us.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，它确实对我们强加了一种纪律。

sentences.en: Do you think that might be good in the long run?
sentences.zh: 你认为从长远来看这可能是件好事吗？

sentences.en: I think it could be good.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能是件好事。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the challenges is even with a Zoom call, people don't like silence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其中一个挑战是，即使在Zoom通话中，人们也不喜欢沉默。

sentences.en: So even though you can't talk over each other, it doesn't stop people necessarily from trying.
sentences.zh: 所以即使你不能压过对方说话，也并不一定能阻止人们尝试这么做。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, what it's really demonstrated is how artificial it comes across when we're trying to have these large meetings, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，这真正证明了当我们试图开这些大型会议时，它是多么的不自然，对吧？

sentences.en: So you're maintaining this total sustained eye contact, which we never do in real meetings.
sentences.zh: 所以你要保持这种完全持续的眼神交流，这我们在真正的会议中是从来不会做的。

sentences.en: In real meetings, we're looking at one person, maybe, or we're looking at our phone.
sentences.zh: 在真正的会议中，我们可能看着一个人，或者看着我们的手机。

sentences.en: You're constantly looking at yourself as well.
sentences.zh: 你也不断地看着自己。

sentences.en: And so you're asking yourself, you know, is that really what my mouth looks like when I talk?
sentences.zh: 所以你会问自己，你知道的，我说话时我的嘴看起来真的是那样吗？

sentences.en: And so it just requires a lot more effort and concentration.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是需要更多的努力和专注。

sentences.en: And when you do them back to back to back without any breaks, it's just exhausting.
sentences.zh: 当你一个接一个、连轴转地进行这些活动而没有任何休息时，简直太累人了。

sentences.en: One of the other behaviors I've read about quite a bit is the fake commute.
sentences.zh: 我读过的另一种经常被提及的行为是“假通勤”。

sentences.en: What is that and how is that helping people?
sentences.zh: 那是什么，它如何帮助人们？

sentences.en: Yeah, I heard about that one a while back, and it seems to have made a resurgence.
sentences.zh: 是的，我前段时间听说过那个，而且它似乎又卷土重来了。

sentences.en: It's this idea of, you know, again, I think it puts some structure and routine in our lives when we have a commute.
sentences.zh: 这是一种想法，你知道的，我认为当我们有通勤时，它再次为我们的生活带来了一些结构和常规。

sentences.en: It represents the beginning and the end of our workday, right, in a really concrete way that we've lost now that so many of us are working from home in the same place that we live.
sentences.zh: 它以一种非常具体的方式代表了我们工作日的开始和结束，随着我们许多人现在在生活的地方居家办公，这种方式已经消失了。

sentences.en: And so I think what the fake commute does is bring this mental structure to the beginning of your day.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为“假通勤”的作用是为你的白天的开始带来这种心理结构。

sentences.en: So it can look like, you know, just walking out of your house, taking a trip around the block, and then coming back.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来可能就像，你知道的，走出你的房子，绕着街区走一圈，然后回来。

sentences.en: And it just gives you, I think, some mental time to prepare and set yourself for your workday.
sentences.zh: 我认为它只是为你提供了一些心理时间来为你的工作日做准备和调整。

sentences.en: Same thing at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 一天结束时也是如此。

sentences.en: It really provides these, I think, bookends to allowing us to really let go and have some boundaries around our work that we've loSt.
sentences.zh: 它真的提供了这些，我认为，首尾呼应的内容，让我们能够真正放手，并在我们已经失去的工作周围建立一些界限。

sentences.en: Based on your expertise in human behavior, what do you think the longer-term consequences of this year of stress and anxiety will be?
sentences.zh: 基于你在人类行为方面的专业知识，你认为这一年压力和焦虑的长期后果会是什么？

sentences.en: Is the concern that a second pandemic is coming, is that warranted?
sentences.zh: 人们担心第二场大流行即将来临，这种担忧是有根据的吗？

sentences.en: You know, I think it's hard to predict the future.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为很难预测未来。

sentences.en: But I will say that if past behavior is the best predictor of future behavior, then these results from the Stress in America surveys over the past year suggest that we could be
sentences.zh: 但我还是要说，如果过去的行为是未来行为的最佳预测指标，那么过去一年来“美国压力调查”的这些结果表明，我们可能会陷入

sentences.en: in pretty significant trouble, that despite the amount of advice that us and others are giving, people are just really struggling with something that none of us were ever prepared
sentences.zh: 相当大的麻烦中，尽管我们和其他人给出了各种建议，人们仍然在艰难地应对我们中没有谁曾经准备好

sentences.en: to deal with for this sustained period of time.
sentences.zh: 在这么长的时间里去处理的事情。

sentences.en: And so I think that we really need to be having larger conversations about our mental health
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们真的需要就我们的心理健康

sentences.en: and our emotional well-being in a way that hasn't gotten elevated yet so that we can start engaging in better coping behaviors.
sentences.zh: 和情绪健康进行更广泛的讨论，这种讨论尚未达到应有的高度，这样我们才能开始采取更好的应对行为。

sentences.en: And that doesn't look just like going to psychotherapy because that's not a solution for everybody,
sentences.zh: 这看起来不仅仅是去做心理治疗，因为那不是每个人的解决方案，

sentences.en: but it's about really meeting people where they're at, whether that's in the workplace, in the schools, in churches, in wherever the case may be.
sentences.zh: 而是要在人们所在的任何地方真正去接触他们，无论是在工作场所、学校、教堂，还是在任何情况下。

sentences.en: I think we really need to start having more of these conversations and reaching out to each other and asking each other, really, you know, how are we doing today?
sentences.zh: 我认为我们真的需要开始进行更多这样的对话，互相伸出援手，真正地问问对方，你知道的，我们今天过得怎么样？

sentences.en: Is the fact that we're hitting a one-year anniversary significant in the sense that people
sentences.zh: 我们迎来一周年纪念日这一事实是否具有重要意义，因为人们

sentences.en: may be reacting even more strongly to the realization that, oh my God, it's really been a whole year that we've been living like this?
sentences.zh: 可能会对“天哪，我们这样生活竟然已经整整一年了”这种认识产生更强烈反应？

sentences.en: Yeah, we know from the research on trauma and PTSD that anniversaries can be pretty significant triggers for individuals who've experienced some level of threats.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们从关于创伤和创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的研究中得知，纪念日对于经历过某种程度威胁的个人来说可能是相当显著的触发因素。

sentences.en: And so it wouldn't surprise me that people are having a particularly hard time right now.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们现在感觉格外艰难，我也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I think it brings on a sense of reflection and reflection can be good, but it's also about our mindset a little bit and having some balance.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会带来一种反思，反思可能是件好事，但这也关乎我们的一点心态以及保持某种平衡。

sentences.en: So I'm hearing a lot of discussion about all the negatives that have happened over the last year and how people have felt like they quote unquote lost a year.
sentences.zh: 所以我听到很多关于过去一年发生的所有负面事情以及人们如何觉得自己“失去了一年”的讨论。

sentences.en: And while it's true that we have lost many milestones, people, jobs, etc., I do think that
sentences.zh: 虽然确实我们失去了许多里程碑、人、工作等，但我确实认为

sentences.en: there has been gains that we've seen in the last year that people can look on and feel some gratitude for.
sentences.zh: 我们在过去一年中看到了人们可以回顾并为此感到感激的收获。

sentences.en: I think the most important being how we, I believe, have come to reevaluate the importance of relationships, both within our family, but with our friends and with our coworkers.
sentences.zh: 我认为最重要的是我们如何重新评估了人际关系的重要性，无论是在我们的家庭内部，还是与我们的朋友和同事之间。

sentences.en: And I do hope that some of that can continue on, that we continue to prioritize and really value
sentences.zh: 我确实希望其中一些能够持续下去，我们继续优先考虑并真正重视

sentences.en: family over things and the things that we realize we could live without for a whole year.
sentences.zh: 家庭胜过物质，以及那些我们意识到没有它们我们也能过上一整年的东西。

sentences.en: And then, you know, just again, reevaluate how we want to live our lives going forward so that we continue to live lives worth living.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，再次重新评估我们希望如何继续生活下去，以便我们能够继续过有价值的生活。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's real interesting how we've become more intimate with the people who are our coworkers.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们与作为同事的人变得更加亲密，这真的很奇妙。

sentences.en: We see their homes, they're on Zooms and their kids come running in with, oh, mom, I just, you know, skinned my knee or things are just happening or the plumber is at the door.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了他们的家，他们在Zoom上开会，他们的孩子跑进来喊着“哦，妈妈，我只是，你知道，擦破了膝盖”或者事情正在发生，或者水管工在门外。

sentences.en: I've got to go.
sentences.zh: 我得走了。

sentences.en: It's just really a completely different feeling.
sentences.zh: 这真的完全是一种不同的感觉。

sentences.en: And I think we're going to see workplace changes.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们将看到职场的变化。

sentences.en: I mean, what are you anticipating that the workplace will be like when the pandemic is declared over?
sentences.zh: 我是说，当疫情被宣布结束时，你预计职场会是什么样子的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's going to really vary depending on probably the field you're in and even maybe the area of the country that you're in.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这会有很大差异，这可能取决于你所在的领域，甚至可能取决于你所在的地区。

sentences.en: But I do think work is fundamentally never going to look quite the same.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，工作从根本上将永远不会完全一样。

sentences.en: We have demonstrated that I think people can effectively work in a more flexible manner.
sentences.zh: 我们已经证明，我认为人们可以以更灵活的方式高效地工作。

sentences.en: And whether that means working from home more frequently, whether that means working slightly more flex hours so that you can take time maybe in the middle of the day to address
sentences.zh: 无论是意味着更频繁地在家工作，还是意味着稍微增加弹性工作时间，以便你可以在一天中间抽出时间来处理

sentences.en: things that before you would have felt like you couldn't, you know, because of the strict
sentences.zh: 那些以前你可能会觉得无法处理的事情，你知道的，因为有严格的

sentences.en: ways that I think all of us had been thinking about how work is, quote unquote, supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们所有人都曾有过的关于工作所谓的“应该”是什么样子的刻板印象。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of those old notions have been demonstrated to be outdated, that they don't really reflect the real world that most of us are living in right now.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为许多旧观念已被证明是过时的，它们并不真正反映我们大多数人现在所处的现实世界。

sentences.en: And so I do think that using technology and having some flexibility and really prioritizing
sentences.zh: 所以，我确实认为利用技术、保持一定的灵活性，并真正以更好的方式优先考虑

sentences.en: work-life balance in a better way will become more of the norm going forward for most people.
sentences.zh: 工作与生活的平衡，在未来将成为大多数人的常态。

sentences.en: One thing that people are thinking about more right now, since we have three very effective
sentences.zh: 现在人们更多思考的一件事是，既然我们有三种非常有效的

sentences.en: vaccines that are getting into people's arms, they're thinking, what's it going to be like when things start to return to normal?
sentences.zh: 疫苗正在注射到人们体内，他们在想，当事情开始恢复正常时会是什么样子？

sentences.en: What did APA survey find about how people feel regarding the idea of going back to seeing friends, eating out, traveling, engaging in those activities where we're going to be
sentences.zh: 美国心理协会（APA）的调查发现，人们对于重新去看望朋友、外出就餐、旅行，参与那些我们将要重新开始的活动有何感受？

sentences.en: seeing more people face-to-face again?
sentences.zh: 再次面对面地看到更多人？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think we're seeing an interesting dichotomy, right, where there's this real desire to want
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为我们看到了一种有趣的对立，对吧，一方面非常渴望

sentences.en: to see our families and have things not look like they do right now, but there's a lot of anxiety about it as well.
sentences.zh: 去看望家人，让生活不再像现在这样，但另一方面对此也有很多焦虑。

sentences.en: So we found that over nearly 50% of adults reported that they felt either uncomfortable or with returning
sentences.zh: 因此我们发现，将近50%的成年人表示，他们感到不舒服，或者对于回归

sentences.en: to life how it was before the pandemic and reporting concerns about sort of re-engaging in these one-to-one face-to-face kinds of conversations.
sentences.zh: 到疫情前那种生活状态感到担忧，并报告说担心重新参与这种一对一的面对面交谈。

sentences.en: And that held true regardless of whether you'd actually had the vaccine or not.
sentences.zh: 而且无论你是否真的接种过疫苗，情况都是如此。

sentences.en: And I think that part of what's driving this anxiety is, again, this level of uncertainty that continues.
sentences.zh: 我认为，驱动这种焦虑的部分原因，再次是这种持续存在的极端不确定性。

sentences.en: Even as we have these three great vaccines, there's still a lot of uncertainty about what's going to happen with these new variants.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们有了这三种极好的疫苗，但对于这些新变异株会发生什么，仍然存在很大的不确定性。

sentences.en: And how long will these vaccines last?
sentences.zh: 这些疫苗能持续多久？

sentences.en: And can someone be asymptomatic?
sentences.zh: 人会无症状感染吗？

sentences.en: And so in the face of all that uncertainty, we become really ineffective at making good risk threat assessments.
sentences.zh: 因此，面对所有这些不确定性，我们在做出良好的风险威胁评估方面变得非常低效。

sentences.en: We have a tendency to either overestimate risk or underestimate risk.
sentences.zh: 我们往往会高估风险或低估风险。

sentences.en: And that then translates into our behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这随后就会转化为我们的行为。

sentences.en: And we have to ask ourselves, is it safe to see friends and family now?
sentences.zh: 我们不得不问自己，现在去看望朋友和家人安全吗？

sentences.en: Is it safe to eat inside that restaurant?
sentences.zh: 在那个餐厅里面吃饭安全吗？

sentences.en: And having to make those decisions over and over and over again, one, it's exhausting.
sentences.zh: 一遍又一遍、反反复复地做出这些决定，首先，这令人筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: But two, you're always not sure if you're putting yourself and your family at risk.
sentences.zh: 但其次，你总是无法确定自己是否在让自己和家人承担风险。

sentences.en: And so I think that's really what's driving a lot of this stress about re-entry.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这确实是驱动这种关于重新融入社会的压力的主要原因。

sentences.en: And yeah, I mean, you raised the question of how you navigate relationships with friends and family members who have different ideas about what it's okay to do now, because there's
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，你提出了如何处理与朋友和家人的关系的问题，他们对于现在做什么才是可以接受的有不同的看法，因为

sentences.en: just so much uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 实在有太多的不确定性。

sentences.en: How best can people navigate making those decisions?
sentences.zh: 人们最好如何去处理这些决定的做出？

sentences.en: And where should they be getting their information so they know what risks are reasonable and what risks are just not?
sentences.zh: 他们应该从哪里获取信息，以便知道哪些风险是合理的，哪些不是？

sentences.en: Yes, certainly we want to be following the best scientific advice that we can find.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，我们希望遵循我们能找到的最佳科学建议。

sentences.en: So that's really institutions like the CDC and the WHO.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是像美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）和世界卫生组织（WHO）这样的机构。

sentences.en: And so following those sorts of recommendations is a good place to start.
sentences.zh: 因此，遵循这些类型的建议是一个很好的开始。

sentences.en: The second is, you know, one, really having some grace for yourself and for others as we're trying to make these decisions.
sentences.zh: 第二是，你知道的，一方面，在试图做出这些决定时，要对自己和他人多一些宽容。

sentences.en: I think we have a tendency to get judgmental just because somebody maybe sees something differently
sentences.zh: 我认为我们往往会带有批判性，仅仅因为某人可能看待事物的角度

sentences.en: than we do, and instead of sort of approaching it with judgment, I think we can approach it
sentences.zh: 与我们不同，与其用批判的态度去对待，不如我认为我们可以用

sentences.en: with grace and that everybody really has their own level of risk that they're comfortable taking.
sentences.zh: 宽容的态度去对待，而且每个人确实都有他们乐于接受的各自的风险水平。

sentences.en: And then you need to sit down with your family or whoever, you know, you sort of interact with and come up with a plan of what you're comfortable with based on your individual risk
sentences.zh: 然后你需要和你的家人，或者任何你知道的与你互动的人坐下来，根据你的个人风险因素

sentences.en: factors and where you, including where you live, and then just unapologetically stick to it when someone challenges you on it.
sentences.zh: 以及你所在的地方（包括你住在哪里），制定一个你觉得舒适的计划，当有人对此提出质疑时，理直气壮地坚持下去。

sentences.en: You can be firm, but friendly.
sentences.zh: 你可以坚定，但要友好。

sentences.en: And I think that's just the approach and flexible because as more information comes in, we need to be able to adapt and maybe make new choices.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是方法，而且要保持灵活性，因为随着更多信息的涌现，我们需要能够适应并可能做出新的选择。

sentences.en: And that's perfectly okay.
sentences.zh: 这完全没有问题。

sentences.en: Maybe this is an unfair question, but what can we expect to see the next time APA goes out and surveys again?
sentences.zh: 也许这是一个不公平的问题，但下次美国心理协会再次进行调查时，我们可以期待看到什么？

sentences.en: I mean, with the vaccines getting out there, should we start to see the stress levels drop?
sentences.zh: 我是说，随着疫苗的普及，我们应该开始看到压力水平下降吗？

sentences.en: I know we'd like to, but do you think that it's likely based on your experience over the past year and just over time?
sentences.zh: 我知道我们希望如此，但根据你过去一年的经验以及时间的推移，你认为这可能吗？

sentences.en: I think for some groups, we're likely to see the stress levels come down.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于某些群体，我们很可能会看到压力水平下降。

sentences.en: It's going to be in particular older adults.
sentences.zh: 特别是老年人群体。

sentences.en: They report some of the lowest levels of stress in the first place, but I think for them, what's been most stressful has been the lack of interacting with family.
sentences.zh: 他们一开始报告的压力水平就最低，但我认为对他们来说，压力最大的是缺乏与家人的互动。

sentences.en: And I think one of the first things we're going to see with the vaccines rolling out is the ability for small families to come back together, for grandparents to see their
sentences.zh: 我认为随着疫苗的推出，我们首先看到的事情之一就是小家庭重新团聚的能力，祖父母得以见到

sentences.en: grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 他们的孙辈。

sentences.en: I do really continue to worry for the four vulnerable groups that we talked about before.
sentences.zh: 我确实仍然为我们之前讨论过的四个弱势群体感到担忧。

sentences.en: I think we've also seen in our research that as kids are going back to school, parents reporting lower levels of stress.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在研究中也发现，随着孩子们重返学校，父母报告的压力水平有所降低。

sentences.en: So the sooner we can get schools safely reopened, I think we'll help that group.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们能越快让学校安全重新开放，我认为就越能帮助那个群体。

sentences.en: But for individuals from communities of color and essential workers, I have strong concerns for their mental well-being going forward if we don't make some systemic changes.
sentences.zh: 但是对于有色人种社区的个人和基本工作者，如果我们不做出一些系统性的改变，我对他们未来的心理健康深表担忧。

sentences.en: These are not individual level changes, but changes within our health care system, within
sentences.zh: 这些不是个人层面的改变，而是我们医疗保健系统内部的改变，

sentences.en: obviously our social system, as well as ensuring that people have resources that they've loSt.
sentences.zh: 显而易见还有我们社会系统内部的改变，以及确保人们拥有他们已经失去的资源。

sentences.en: I think unless those things really happen at a more population health level, then we're going to continue to see individuals really reporting that they're struggling.
sentences.zh: 我认为，除非这些事情真正在更大的人口健康层面上发生，否则我们将继续看到个人不断报告他们在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: On balance, more optimism or more pessimism right now?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，现在是更乐观还是更悲观？

sentences.en: I, you know, I've always leaned towards pessimism.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道的，我一直倾向于悲观。

sentences.en: Obviously, I said it firSt.
sentences.zh: 显然，我先说出来的。

sentences.en: So it's such a Freudian slip on my part.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是我无意中说漏嘴了。

sentences.en: I'm an optimist, darn it.
sentences.zh: 我其实是个乐观主义者，该死。

sentences.en: But no, I'm feeling optimistic, you know, I think that there are more people out there that want the vaccine that don't, although I do think vaccine hesitancy is still an issue.
sentences.zh: 但说真的，我感觉很乐观，你知道的，我认为想要疫苗的人比不想要的多，尽管我确实认为疫苗犹豫仍然是一个问题。

sentences.en: And I think that it needs to be addressed again at a larger level and within the communities that community leaders come forward, they're vocal and they're visual about, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为这需要在更大的层面上以及在社区内部得到解决，社区领导人要站出来，大声且直观地表明

sentences.en: accepting the vaccine and providing that opportunity.
sentences.zh: 他们接受疫苗并提供这种机会。

sentences.en: And I think hopefully that these conversations will continue and maybe even elevate now that we're moving forward and we're less focused just on our physical health.
sentences.zh: 我希望这些对话能够继续下去，甚至可能在现在我们向前发展且不那么只关注身体健康的时候得到提升。

sentences.en: I think the natural pivot will have to be to talking more broadly about our mental health.
sentences.zh: 我认为自然的转变将不得不转向更广泛地谈论我们的心理健康。

sentences.en: And you can't fix something until you acknowledge and are aware that it's an issue.
sentences.zh: 在承认并意识到这是一个问题之前，你是无法解决它的。

sentences.en: And so I think that's where we need to get to.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这就是我们需要达到的状态。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for joining us today, Dr. Wright.
sentences.zh: 好的，赖特博士，谢谢你今天加入我们。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure talking with you as always.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，和你交谈非常愉快。

sentences.en: And I hope to see you in the office again one of these days.
sentences.zh: 希望过几天能在办公室再见到你。

sentences.en: Yes, let's hope so.
sentences.zh: 是的，但愿如此。

sentences.en: You can find links to APA's COVID-19 information and resources, as well as our Stress in America surveys, on our website at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 APA.org 上找到指向美国心理协会 COVID-19 信息和资源的链接，以及我们的美国压力调查。

sentences.en: And you can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology there or on speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在那里或在 speakingofpsychology.org 上找到往期的《心理学对话》节目。

sentences.en: Or you can get them on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以在 Apple、Stitcher 或你获取播客的任何地方收听它们。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, email us at speakingofpsychology at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有意见或想法，请发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology 加上 @APA.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 那是 speakingofpsychology，全部连在一起，@APA.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学对话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的声音编辑是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是代表美国心理协会的金·米尔斯。
